top_story_title: Another week of exploited edge appliances — Ivanti, Cisco and Palo Alto Networks named, BeyondTrust joins
top_story_summary: Dark Reading reports that vulnerabilities in edge devices from Ivanti, Cisco and Palo Alto Networks all came under attack this week, and that a zero-day in BeyondTrust Remote Support now continues the same pattern. The report is a trend piece: it names the vendors whose edge gear was targeted but does not publish CVE IDs, affected models or fixed releases for them, so nothing here identifies a specific build you can check a device against.
top_actions: Inventory internet-facing edge devices from Ivanti, Cisco and Palo Alto Networks and record the exact running version of each; this report names no versions, so the vendor advisory is the only authority.

Check each vendor's PSIRT/advisory page for current exploited-in-the-wild entries against those running versions, and schedule upgrades to the vendor's stated fixed release inside the change window, HA pair secondary first.
Remove management access (HTTPS/SSH/API) from any internet-facing interface now; restrict administration to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network. This does not wait for a patch.
Enforce phishing-resistant MFA on all administrative and remote-access accounts, and remove shared local admin accounts.

Where a device is found affected by an actively exploited flaw, terminate active sessions, revoke session tokens, and rotate local admin credentials, API keys, certificates and VPN pre-shared keys after the upgrade — a pre-patch compromise survives it.
executive_summary: Edge devices from Ivanti, Cisco and Palo Alto Networks were reported under attack this week alongside a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day; the report names vendors but no CVEs, models or fixed releases — check each vendor's advisory against your running versions.

Palo Alto Networks published CVE-2026-0307, a medium-severity local privilege escalation in the GlobalProtect app. The advisory listing states no fixed build here; consult the PSIRT page before planning the client rollout.
Quiet cycle for device advisories: 5 items collected in the 24h window, 2 relevant to network infrastructure. Two phishing-research items and one cloud AI-agent post were filtered out as off-scope.
Check Point described AI-agent protection integrated with Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise — a vendor AI defence rather than a network-device issue; it is recorded in the AI defences section.
key_actions: **Multiple** — Identify every internet-facing Ivanti, Cisco and Palo Alto Networks edge device from the asset inventory, filtered by model and running version.

**Multiple** — Check each vendor's PSIRT advisories for current actively exploited entries matching those versions, and apply the vendor's stated fixed release or documented workaround; do not act on a version number not published by the vendor.

ai_defenses.solution: Check Point on Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise — AI-specific risk assessment and real-time, context-aware protection for AI agents
ai_defenses.what_it_does: Extends Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise agent control plane with AI-specific risk assessment and real-time, context-aware protection, covering AI agents from discovery through runtime. The source describes the integration points rather than a separately named product.
